question:
Who opens the door
when your own is shut?
next_voice: Next, in Part Three: the rope.

beats.text: Her father's door was the last door she had left.
beats.scene: A heavy closed wooden door in the rough stone wall of a poor farmhouse at dusk; the long shadow of a woman holding a small child falls across the door. Nobody visible, only the shadow.

beats.text: She came home to Laviano with her little son, and nothing else.
Her stepmother would not have them in the house.
beats.scene: Inside the dark doorway of a poor medieval farmhouse, a severe older peasant woman in a dark headscarf stands blocking the way, one hand on the door frame, hard light from outside on her face, cold expression. Ordinary and human, not a villain.

beats.text: And her father turned her away.
Tradition says she sat under a fig tree in the garden, and wept.
She was tempted to go back to the only life she knew.
beats.scene: A crossroads at night seen from behind a young woman in a dark hooded cloak carrying a sleeping small child on her shoulder: one road leads back toward a distant castle with lit windows on a hill, the other into darkness toward a far town on a ridge. Her face is not visible.

beats.text: Instead she took her son and walked to Cortona, to the Franciscan friars.
beats.scene: Dawn: seen from far behind, a young woman in a dark hooded cloak walks up a long steep road toward a walled hilltop town, holding a small boy by the hand, pale light breaking over the ridge, long shadows behind them. Their faces are not visible.

beats.text: There, two women of the town opened their door to her.
